sections.name: File setup, solutionName, STAGE_LABEL, newProjectFlag, accountNames
sections.title: Imports and small label helpers
sections.what: Brings in the icon, the link component, the shared labels and data types, the location helper, and the priority helpers. Also defines helpers that name a solution, a stage, the new-project flag, and the account names attached to a signal.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps label wording in one place so every card and detail view says the same thing.
sections.watch_out: A stage value not in the stage list is shown as it is stored, so new stage names would appear unformatted.

sections.name: StrengthMeter
sections.title: Strength meter
sections.what: Shows signal strength as one to three filled bars with a word label, and either the word alone or the word with the score.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a quick visual read of how well supported a signal is.
sections.watch_out: The bars expect the strength label to be weak, moderate or strong. Any other value shows empty bars.

sections.name: SignalCard
sections.title: Signal card
sections.what: Shows one signal as a clickable card with its type, priority score, flags for new project, megaproject, provisional mapping and pending classification, title, summary, optional relevance match, strength, capex, tier, solution, clients, country and source count.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives enough detail to choose a signal without opening it.
sections.watch_out: When no relevance percentage is given, the card shows keyword match, which users might read as a scored result.

sections.name: Section
sections.title: Labelled section box
sections.what: Draws a titled block used in the detail view. It can be marked in red for hypothesis sections.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It keeps the detail sections looking alike.

sections.name: Field
sections.title: Labelled field
sections.what: Shows a labelled value in the detail view, or a grey fallback phrase when the value is missing.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. It keeps missing information visibly marked.
sections.watch_out: An empty text value is treated as missing, so it shows the fallback phrase.

sections.name: SignalDetail (part 1)
sections.title: Signal detail, top half
sections.what: Builds the full signal view: a heading with type and status, flags, four headline figures (priority, strength, capex with its band, and tier with evidence confidence), a warning for inferred whitespace signals, the observed summary, a clearly labelled advisory hypothesis, and the primary solution with its rationale. Mapping fields follow. A helper here turns an evidence item into a source record, and its use is not visible in the packet.
sections.why: Likely reason: separates reported facts from advisory guesses, so users do not treat a hypothesis as a confirmed client need.
sections.watch_out: The inference warning appears only for whitespace signals, so other inferred content gets no warning here.

sections.name: SignalDetail (part 2)
sections.title: Detail panels for evidence and classification
sections.what: Shows the lower panels of an opened signal: how the codebook classified it, the priority breakdown using the owner's weights, the sources and quotes behind it, capex, whether it counts as a new project, its Yard link, its map locations, and research notes. Where data is missing, each panel says so in plain words instead of leaving a blank.
sections.why: Likely reason: the owner needs to see where each fact came from and whether it is missing, so the panels state gaps explicitly.
sections.watch_out: Capex is shown as Unknown rather than zero when no figure exists, so code changes must keep missing values separate from a real zero.

sections.name: SignalDetail (part 3)
sections.title: Review status buttons
sections.what: Shows one button for each review state (new, reviewing, dismissed, resolved). The current state is marked as pressed and cannot be clicked again, and all buttons are disabled while a save is running.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the reviewer record progress on each signal. The code does not state this directly.
sections.watch_out: The labels come from a shared status list, so a new status must be added there as well as in the status type, or it will not appear here.

summary: Shows opportunity signals as clickable cards and as a detailed view with the evidence, the hypothesis, the mapping, and the reasons behind each tier.
purpose: Lets an analyst scan signals quickly and then judge one in depth, separating reported facts from advisory guesses.
why: Likely reason: the detail view separates observed facts, inferred whitespace, and advisory solution ideas, so a hypothesis is not mistaken for a confirmed need.
how: Builds a card for each signal with its key figures and flags. The detail view shows headline figures, warnings for inferred signals, the observed summary, a labelled hypothesis, the primary solution with its rationale, and a set of mapping fields. Small helpers draw the strength bars and labelled fields.
inputs: One signal, a name lookup function, solutions, accounts, the current weights, the codebook of labels, the relevance score if any, and callbacks for opening sources and changing status.
outputs: A clickable signal card and a detailed signal view with fields, sections and the source and status actions. Only the first six sections are shown in this packet.
risks: A signal with incomplete classification shows placeholder text, which can look like a finished result. The warning for inferred signals applies only to one signal kind. A helper for building source records is defined but its use is not visible in the packet.
debug: If a field is missing, check the mapping data and the classification status. If the strength bars look empty, check the strength label value. If a card shows keyword match, the relevance score was not given. If labels look raw, check the codebook.
